title: Two WWII 'rescue' films: one true, the other a whitewash
summary: On August 15, the anniversary of Japan's WWII surrender, two maritime rescue films were released with contrasting messages. "Dongji Rescue" recounts the true story of the 1942 Lisbon Maru tragedy, highlighting Chinese fishermen who risked their lives to save British POWs from Japanese cruelty. In contrast, "Yukikaze" portrays an invading fleet as heroes, effectively whitewashing history. These films reflect the ongoing contestation of historical narratives and influence how the past is remembered or rewritten
